## October 27 — clarify how visitors keep a moment

**Finding:** the Field Companion's main Save button was followed by visible guidance about “export” and “auto-save,” terms that did not match the ordinary action label and could make a first-time user wonder what to do.

**Change:** the app home gives one short action: download a copy before closing to keep the moment. Station setup explains that sounds and notes stay in the page until the visitor downloads them. The optional sound-context note uses “saved note.” Replacing a session and reaching the temporary sound limit explain the outcome without mentioning JSON or exports. The post-save note says the downloaded copy stays on the device and is not sent to Talk2Nature or added to research. The dedicated research JSON control remains under the optional Advanced disclosure.

**Verification:** all 185 Python tests passed (one intentional skip), and all 133 Node tests passed. The local noindex build produced 143 pages plus 404; the site checker validated 144 HTML documents and 7,477 links. Installed desktop Chrome via Playwright rendered the home and Station at 320×740 and 390×844 CSS pixels; document widths matched each viewport, the feedback link remained above the fixed dock, and the main Save button fit in the first post-session review screen. The microphone-free rehearsal completed through a real ZIP download with zero microphone calls and no JavaScript errors. Screenshots were visually inspected.

**Release and live read-back:** PR [#472](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/pull/472) merged to `main` as [`56f2006`](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/commit/56f2006d1ab47a9b957175155d8d25cd45d89083). Pages run [#40550996297](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/actions/runs/40550996297) passed build, publish-boundary checks, deployment and its live-route verifier. Fresh TLS-verified reads returned HTTP 200 for `/app/` and `/app/station/`; both contained the new copy.

**Limits:** these are maintainer-run desktop-browser checks with emulated phone dimensions and invented practice material, not physical-phone, assistive-technology or independent first-time-user evidence. No real recording or participant data was used. The named physical-phone check and authorized, uncoached newcomer walkthrough remain open; no tester was contacted. Keep the five-track goal active; AutoResearch and real-data admission remain **NOT READY**.

## October 26 — add a bounded plant–insect review route for research groups

**Question:** can the university evaluation page invite insect and plant sensory researchers to critique a concrete receiver-response result without implying that plants intentionally communicate?

**Evidence reviewed:** the eLife version-of-record article (January 5, 2026), its Abstract, Results, Discussion and Methods sections, and the published peer reviews and author responses. In controlled choices, female Egyptian cotton leafworm moths preferred the drought-plant playback side when no plant was present, but preferred the silent side when hydrated tomato plants were offered; deafening removed the playback preference. The main choice setup used 60 clicks/min, while the authors measured up to 20 clicks/min from 45 seedlings over 50 hours; a separate 30-click/min long-arena experiment used a different setup. The reviews discuss playback-rate realism, effect-size presentation and species generalization. The authors describe the drought clicks as likely cues, not signals evolved to convey a message.

**Change:** added a fourth optional card to `/community/university/` and updated the evaluation brief. It asks what the controlled choices support and what context/rate differences constrain interpretation. It links the existing plant–moth evidence note, the article's public peer reviews and the established public scientific-review form. The boundary states that the work covers one moth species and one plant species, and that any submitted review is public. This is an invitation to critique literature, not a claim of plant language, a request for experiments/playback, or an external endorsement.

**Release:** PR [#453](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/pull/453) merged to `main` as [`03783ff`](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/commit/03783ff4ea4a7509790c94076fa980c296d61129). Manual Pages run [#40238793798](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/actions/runs/40238793798) passed the repository and browser-tool tests, Android checks, public build, publish-boundary checks, deployment and workflow live verifier.

**Live read-back:** a cache-bypassing TLS-verified request returned HTTP 200 for `/community/university/`. The served page includes the plant–moth bounded question, the eLife peer-review link and the warning that submitted reviews are public GitHub issues. Its canonical points to itself, robots allow indexing, and the route is present in the valid 140-URL sitemap.

**Validation and limits:** all 175 Python tests passed with one intentional skip; all 127 Node tests passed. Local and public builds each generated 140 pages plus 404; checks passed for 141 HTML documents, with 7,306 local links and 7,447 public links, and all 140 public routes reachable. Chrome device emulation rendered the university route at 390 CSS pixels and measured widths at 320, 390 and 1440: document width matched each viewport; all four review cards fit without horizontal overflow. This is browser emulation, not a physical-phone test. No dataset files, audio, figures, code or model were acquired; no experiment or outside reviewer was contacted. The route invites critique of a context-dependent result from one moth/one plant study; it does not establish independent scientific validation, plant language or general communication.

## October 25 — correct offline status during service-worker replacement

**Question:** why did the public Field Companion show both an update-ready notice and an offline-setup failure, and was the offline shell actually unavailable?

**Observed and traced:** the published app home displayed “Update ready” and “Offline setup did not complete” at the same time. In `web/assets/app.js`, every `redundant` service-worker state unconditionally wrote the failure message. The [W3C Service Workers specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/service-workers/) uses `redundant` both when a worker is replaced and when an install fails. The app already asks its active worker whether the exact offline shell is ready, so this lifecycle event alone was not proof that offline setup had failed.

**Change and checks:** the redundant-worker handler now checks the active shell and preserves the truthful state: ready when its complete allowlist is present, repair guidance when an active shell is incomplete, and an install-failure message only when no active worker exists. Added focused cases for all three states. The clean local first-visit browser check showed “Offline tools are optional” with no error; this check did not create an offline registration. Python tests passed (170, one skipped), Node tests passed (122), and the local noindex build/check passed (139 HTML pages, 7,090 links). The app helper remains in the existing offline asset allowlist.

**Publication and read-back:** [PR #394](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/pull/394) merged as [`2f083ad`](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/commit/2f083ade986b3590599719b86ee592d83d53c749). Pages run [#40147458630](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/actions/runs/40147458630) passed both test suites, the public build and boundaries check, deployment, and live-route/crawl-metadata verification. A fresh TLS-verified read-back returned HTTP 200 for the mobile home and its versioned `app.js` and `app-update.mjs`; both scripts contain the deployed readiness resolver.

**Limits and next step:** the replacement/failure branches were exercised through the helper's tests, not a physical-phone service-worker lifecycle. The local clean-first-visit preview confirms optional offline setup starts without an error, but does not test an existing active shell being replaced in the live browser. Existing tabs may continue on a service-worker-controlled revision until they are normally closed and reopened. Next, verify the replacement state in a clean or refreshed browser session, then continue the outside first-use and physical-device gates. No recordings were made, uploaded or admitted.

## October 25 — walk through the published zero-command rehearsal

**Question:** can a first-use visitor try the Shared moments path without configuration or microphone access, and does the app accurately describe what the practice result is?

**Live walkthrough:** on the published `mode=companion` route, the preset showed “Whole moment · 30 seconds” and left animal identity at “Not sure yet.” One tap on “Try without a microphone” started a clearly labeled synthetic session and did not request microphone access. Ending it after about 1.8 seconds produced a “Partial observation window” recap labeled “Invented practice audio”; the page said the audio remained temporary and should be saved before leaving. In a second live run of the `mode=demo` route, the same one-tap practice started without microphone access, accepted a “Movement” marker at about 3 seconds, and stopped at 4.9 seconds. ## October 24 — choose a first species by scientific task, not dataset size

**Question:** which animal and existing resource give Talk2Nature the most useful first research foothold?

**Decision:** keep the Field Companion species-neutral. Prioritize the Egyptian fruit-bat corpus for vocal-context research because its primary descriptor reports 293,238 short recordings and 91,080 video-derived annotations with emitter/addressee and behavior/context information ([Prat et al., 2017](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2017.143)). The strict participant graph has a 95.56% largest component. A new caller-specific aggregate check excludes 122 mixed-caller source files, retains 99.26% of the paper-filtered annotations, and leaves every context represented by at least eight callers. This makes a narrow new-caller question plausible for review, while exact paper fold membership and whole-animal independence remain unresolved. Honeybee waggle data are the clearest known signal-to-receiver candidate, but the signal is movement, its core association is already published, and the archive is one site ([Dormagen et al., 2023](https://doi.org/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgad275)). Budgerigars remain a possible usability cohort if access and qualified review become available; the reviewed household corpus search did not find a public parrot audio dataset with independent event-aligned context labels.

**Next gate:** ask independent bat-behavior and ML/statistical reviewers whether a caller-held-out, whole-file split is a defensible new-caller test beyond the paper's reported subject-independent folds; determine whether role uncertainty and chamber/session/treatment effects change that conclusion. Verify exact paper folds or leave them explicitly unresolved. If no non-duplicative question survives review, record a no-go and use a non-semantic sound-identification task only to test the app/data pipeline. No audio acquisition, model training, recruitment or translator claim is authorized by this checkpoint. AutoResearch remains **NOT READY**.

## October 14 — full review of parrot touchscreen ergonomics

**Question:** what does the CHI 2024 parrot touchscreen paper support for Talk2Nature's mobile product, and what remains a separate animal-computer-interaction question?

**Evidence reviewed:** read the full published article text, Sections 1–7, from the University of Glasgow record and PDF. The study enrolled 20 adult home-kept parrots and 17 completed its trained tablet task. On its 10.1-inch Galaxy Tab A setup, hit rate increased from 19.29% at 40 dp to 47.08% at 130 dp; target distance was not significant, and touch-point precision did not significantly differ by width. The paper's caregiver survey/pilot, participant screening, welfare procedures, task, analysis and limitations were reviewed. Figures were not visually reanalyzed; no raw data, code, supplements or independent analysis were inspected.

**Product and rights decision:** this is tablet ergonomics evidence, not a phone specification, communication test or justification for automated playback. Keep the current Field Companion human-operated and passive. Any parrot-operated enrichment interface is a separate product/welfare project requiring qualified ACI and avian review. The repository lists CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and “Data Availability Statement: No”; the catalog adds only an original summary and metadata-only paper record, with no article files or study data.

Read Sections 1–4 of its open full text through PubMed Central and compared its interpretation with the already-reviewed 2016, 2017 and 2022 primary studies and Schlenker et al. (2024). The critique agrees the experiments show receiver sensitivity to call order and different responses to one-source versus two-source AR, but disputes the Core-Merge/hierarchical-syntax inference. It offers finite-list and finite-state/concatenation accounts and flags the 2017 cross-species sequence as a result a unified account must explain. This is a published conceptual critique, not a new experiment or a consensus statement.

**Data check:** rechecked the official Figshare v2 API for item 18007046 v1. It currently returns CC BY 4.0 and per-file MD5 values for the two 2,058-byte tables and two R scripts. It verified the two 64-row tables align on all flock-trial metadata and agree on whether each trial has any outcome event. For the binary table, the natural one-source 1A-R treatment had approach in 13/16 flock trials and wing-flicking in 15/16; the other treatments had 2–3/16 and 1–4/16 respectively. The aggregate report emits no rows, dates, caller IDs, locations or audio. It does not fit the deposited mixed-effects models, reproduce adjusted contrasts, or identify a communication mechanism.

## October 14 — expand the Japanese-tit reviewer packet with an adjacent receiver study

**Question:** does the 2025 Carolina-wren/great-tit playback add evidence about cross-family receiver responses, and can it support claims about call-order decoding?

**Evidence reviewed:** source 268 was rechecked against the publisher-indexed Methods, Results and Discussion passages and the University of Western Australia repository abstract, publication record and article-license metadata. Direct ScienceDirect retrieval returned HTTP 403; full article files, figures, supplementary material and complete statistical details were not reviewed.

**Finding and limits:** the study used 96 wild great tits across six treatments. Approach differed between calls and controls but not among call treatments; wing-flicking was more frequent after complete FME–D sequences than after D-only calls or controls. No reversed-order condition was tested, so the result is adjacent cross-family receiver-response evidence, not evidence of Japanese-tit order decoding or an independent replication. The authors note that the Carolina-wren component functions remain unconfirmed and that the D-only comparison was not duty-cycle matched; the stimulus set also reduces four callers to two constructed tracks per call treatment.

## October 14: budgerigar dataset-alignment correction and evidence refresh

**Question:** does the public Dryad deposit provide synchronized vocal events and observed social behavior, and did the earlier summary describe the recorded social group correctly?

**Evidence reviewed:** the [primary article](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10265024/) Methods on animal housing, experimental outline, audio and video recording; the [official Dryad version history, file inventory and README](https://datadryad.org/dataset/doi:10.5061/dryad.fttdz08xr); and Dryad's [reuse policy](https://datadryad.org/help/guides/reuse). The Dryad README describes the interobserver workbook and its recoded subset. The workbook itself was not acquired or inspected.

**Correction and finding:** an October 11 note incorrectly called the videos “home-flock” recordings. The paper describes separate video sessions of the newly formed experimental flocks. Contact calls were collected from an isolated focal bird in separate 55-minute sessions, with visual but not acoustic contact to flockmates; social videos were two 80-minute sessions per flock per recording block. The deposit lists derived call-feature tables and social/proximity coding with overlapping group/date/block fields, but no source call WAVs or shared call/event timestamps. It is a protocol/schema near-match, not an event-level sound-to-behavior benchmark. The README documents an interobserver recoding subset; no reliability value was calculated, and none is claimed. The paper reports age-bounded differences in vocal diversity and affiliative ties while measured plasticity/convergence were similar; these findings do not establish call meaning.

**Rights and decision:** Dryad's policy states data deposits use CC0. The article separately declares CC BY 4.0; the included R scripts have no separately verified software license. No files were downloaded, no code was run, and the resource remains metadata-only. Corrected `content/research.json`, `content/sources.json`, `research/resources.json`, `docs/COLLECTION.md`, `docs/MODEL_DATA_DECISION.md` and `docs/RESEARCH_BACKLOG.md`; added a page-scope regression in `tests/test_site.py`. Next: prioritize a resource with source recordings and independently timed behavior labels; any aggregate analysis of this deposit would require an explicit unit, exact join/missingness audit and qualified review.

## October 13 fungal electrophysiology source and rights follow-up

**Question:** what did the 2026 oyster-fungus propagation paper measure, and can its linked data be safely reused or reproduced?

**Finding:** the primary paper reports approximately 15 days of 1 Hz recording from eight spatially ordered differential channels on one *Pleurotus ostreatus*-colonised substrate. Its lead–lag analysis is evidence reported by the paper for slow electrical propagation consistent with ionic waves. It is not a receiver-response experiment or evidence of decoded language. The eight channels are spatial subsamples of one specimen, and the Methods do not describe external stimulation or a sham/uncolonised-substrate comparison.

**Provenance and rights:** the paper cites Zenodo DOI [10.5281/zenodo.4430968](https://zenodo.org/records/4430968). The official record is v1, created in 2021, lists one 413.2 MB ZIP and provider MD5 `ae00e6ace4114f8ca33572b4930c41b4`, and displays no dataset license. The record does not identify which archive member contains the paper's 15-day, eight-channel series. The article and dataset now have separate resource records; the UWE repository identifies the paper as CC BY 4.0, which does not grant rights to the dataset.

**Change and limits:** updated the fungal research note and added the separate article/data records. No archive was downloaded, no checksum was computed locally, no data were analyzed, and no independent specialist reviewed the paper. Before any reproduction, resolve the file mapping and terms, then obtain mycology/electrophysiology review of independent biological replication, controls and environmental logging. **Finding:** full PMC article text and Table 1 report one *Fusarium oxysporum* strain (NEU 195) and a significant pre-induction PSD difference of about 1,604.752% between 24 fungal and 8 non-inoculated electrode-pair records (p<0.001). The main text reviewed does not establish that electrode-pair records are independent biological replicates. The post-induction drug/carrier comparisons each report n=3 and are nonsignificant (p=.327, .391, .580 and .116). DMSO reproduces the calcimycin pattern and is considered a likely electrode confound; the sodium-azide series has a water-control anomaly. This is specialized extracellular electrophysiology, not evidence of a fungal message or semantic code.

**Rights and change:** updated the existing research note, source records and separate paper, dataset and code resources. The [Mendeley v1 record](https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/srkxbkh6sp/1) displays CC BY 4.0, but its visible Files section lists no file entries. The article identifies supplementary Method S1; its bytes and component-specific license remain unreviewed. No dataset, supplement or code was downloaded or executed, and no result was reproduced. AutoResearch remains **NOT READY**.

**Next gate:** resolve the exact dataset manifest and independent-culture structure; review the supplement and reconcile its Method S1 data-statement pointer with the software table's Document S2 code reference and terms. Obtain mycology/electrophysiology review before any acquisition or reproduction. The evidence page remains an original summary with canonical metadata, sitemap inclusion and crawlability checks; this does not establish search indexing or ranking.

## October 13 Android Station capture-deadline hardening

**Question:** does the Android prototype's selected 1-, 4- or 8-hour cap still get checked if the microphone stops delivering audio frames?

**Finding and change:** the capture loop previously used a blocking `AudioRecord.read()` and compared the limit only with processed audio duration. A stalled read could therefore postpone the app's next time-limit check. Added a monotonic `SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()` deadline, bounded each audio read to samples fitting before that deadline, and switched to non-blocking reads with a short idle wait. The [Android clock reference](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/SystemClock) documents that `elapsedRealtime()` is monotonic and includes sleep; the [AudioRecord reference](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/AudioRecord) documents that `READ_NON_BLOCKING` returns immediately and may return zero samples. Added deterministic deadline arithmetic and eight-hour maximum tests. This is a source-level safety improvement, not proof of an exact stop time on every device.

**Validation:** Android core checks pass; all 107 Node tests and 114 Python tests pass; `git diff --check` passes. This host has no Android SDK, emulator or `adb`, so Gradle package/lint checks and physical-device behavior are not locally verified; the repository pull-request workflow runs Android lint and debug/release assembly. No microphone, recording, deployment or research data was used.

**Release:** PR [#102](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/pull/102) merged as [`7552b6d`](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/commit/7552b6d2ee7247a689d4d239b9b60eb467ab4709). The public-checks workflow passed, including Android lint, debug/release assembly, release-boundary checks and the site build/check. No Pages deployment occurred because the change is Android-only.

**Next:** test limit timing, screen lock, calls and interruption on a named physical device before describing this as field-ready. The broad evidence, app, open-source, SEO and resources goal remains active.

## October 13 common-endophyte network evidence note

**Question:** does a recent plant–fungus experiment change what Talk2Nature can responsibly say about communication through fungal networks? **Evidence reviewed:** Waschk et al., *Evidence for resource transfer via common endophyte networks*, Scientific Reports 16, article 26111 (2026), including its full article, methods, limitations, data-availability and CC BY 4.0 rights statement. The paper reports a split-plate Arabidopsis experiment with three endophytes and stable-isotope measurements. Among its reported outcomes, *Fusarium temperatum* treatments showed 55% higher amino-acid-derived 15N in receiver plants and 38% higher biomass than controls; *Trichoderma viride* showed a smaller 13C enrichment (+2.83%). The study measures resource and physiological outcomes, not a sender message, receiver interpretation or communication.

**Change and rights:** added an original note, two source records, separate paper/data/code catalog entries, a multimodal learning-path link and a regression that preserves the communication and rights boundaries. The official GitLab API pins the current `main` tree to commit `5b4ea51c038213e62feb6580daa5a48ccbfa32ff` (2025-12-04) and lists `CEN.csv` (12,643 bytes), `isotope_analysis.R` (35,976 bytes) and `physiology_analysis.R` (13,080 bytes). The project API declares no license and the inspected root contains no README or license file. The paper is CC BY 4.0; dataset and code rights are separately unresolved. No dataset, code, paper asset or supplement was downloaded, executed or redistributed. No field location was mapped because the study reports no field collection or study-site location.

**Verification and limits:** 105 Python tests and 107 Node tests passed; the catalog validates 101 resources; `git diff --check` passed. ## October 13 Horizon Europe call fit and status check

**Question:** does the Horizon Europe HORIZON-NATURE-2027-02-05 call offer a credible funding path for Talk2Nature, and is it confirmed open today?

**Evidence reviewed:** the official REA call schedule and general applicant guidance, plus pages 13–15 and 144–147 of the official Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027 Part 14. The work programme schedules opening on October 13, 2026 and a deadline of January 14, 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. It allocates €16 million to the topic and expects three projects at €5–6 million each, as a lump-sum research-and-innovation action. The scope is policy-specific: the EU Pollinators Monitoring Scheme, soil biodiversity under the Soil Monitoring Law, or Water Framework Directive monitoring. It expects scalable, cost-effective methods, demonstrations, species identification/quantification, relevant DNA libraries/genomic methods, and FAIR-by-design data. General REA guidance says most calls require at least three organisations from three different EU or associated countries, including one EU member; call-specific portal terms control. On October 13 the direct Funding & Tenders topic URL returned HTTP 200 with a generic JavaScript shell, but no topic record, submission state or application form was exposed in the direct response; browser-rendered status remains unverified.

**Decision:** no current application fit. Talk2Nature has an experimental passive audio observation/annotation workflow, not a validated statutory monitoring method, species-counting system, DNA workflow or Water Framework Directive tool; it has no confirmed scientific lead, applicant entity or eligible consortium. A bounded software or interoperability contribution could be considered only if a qualified consortium demonstrates a need and the workflow is tested for that use. The official Funding & Tenders topic page could not be retrieved during this check, so the actual submission status is unverified despite the scheduled opening date. Do not label the opportunity open until the live portal confirms it. No registration, outreach, expense or application was made.

## October 12: cross-species speech-encoder transfer evidence

**Question:** do human-speech encoders carry useful structure into animal vocalizations, and does that show language-like understanding?

**Evidence reviewed:** the complete arXiv v1 HTML and version/license metadata for Arias-Vergara et al., source 218. The study compares 15 frozen encoders on caller identification and call-type classification across four species. It reports speech-pretrained representations significantly ahead in three of seven comparisons, with no significant difference in four; multilingual and animal-domain pretraining show no systematic advantage. Crucially, some caller-ID folds share individuals across partitions because a session was divided into blocks. The session-independent sensitivity results are lower. The manuscript license is CC BY 4.0; source corpora, code and model weights have separate rights.

**Change:** added an original indexable note, a metadata-only paper resource, a source record, and a link in the model-transfer learning path. The atlas location status remains pending because the reused corpora need original-source location review. No files were copied or acquired, no code or models were run, and no author was contacted.

**Checks and release:** 90 Python tests and 98 Node tests pass; the resource validator accepts 62 records. The public build generates 90 pages plus 404; the site checker verifies 91 HTML files, 4,228 links and 90 reachable public pages. The live note, resource directory and sitemap returned HTTP 200; the note has its expected canonical and `index,follow`, and the sitemap lists 90 URLs including the note. PR [#53](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/pull/53) merged as `319942e86ee270f26d1678a267296e6ebc32536b` and deployed through successful [Pages run #38299565431](https://github.com/Metivity/talk2nature/actions/runs/38299565431).

**Limits and next decision:** this arXiv record does not establish peer review, and the study tests acoustic labels, not independently observed context or message meaning. A bounded exact-title/ID search on GitHub, Zenodo and OpenReview returned no official code/data or venue match; it does not prove none exists. Independent reproduction and specialist review remain absent; AutoResearch is **NOT READY**. Keep the record metadata-only unless an official release or concrete reproduction need emerges; then have a bioacoustic-methods reviewer assess the caller split before considering a bounded run. Search Console indexing was not refreshed after deployment.

## October 2: media/model lineage continuation

Extended the private foundation to schema v2: immutable synthetic audio/video descriptors, clock alignment, frozen model specifications and inputs, and invented result records. The graph now connects sources → frozen study → session → observation → media/alignment → reviewed release → model specification → result. Exact API and migration boundaries are in `docs/MEDIA_LINEAGE.md`. The owner graph uses readable relationship names; these are API-backed research records, not a new consumer upload feature.

All new routes preserve exact owner authorization, CSRF, bounded JSON and synthetic-only admission. Media and alignment membership freeze at observation review. Model specifications require reviewed training permission, matching release/media fingerprints, complete grouped splits and explicit alignment for every multimodal input. Outputs retain probabilities/abstention/calibration separately from human labels and must fit the relevant validity interval. No bytes, object URL, upload grant, playback, model execution or real biological result was added.

Withdrawal redacts media/alignment metadata, invalidates all dependent runs, redacts their results even on other inputs, revokes releases and removes the observation in one transaction. Failure injection verifies full rollback. Opaque provenance tombstones remain private for reconciliation. SQLite and PostgreSQL migrations preserve existing rows; runtime does not silently migrate an old schema. Recovery understands both table inventories and includes lineage tombstones.

Local/public builds passed (51 HTML pages, 1,638 / 1,690 links), and the private UI script passed syntax checking. ## October 12 continuation: deepen the plant–insect acoustic evidence note — local candidate

Confirmed that the active integrated goal already spans research collection, the phone application, open-source quality, technical SEO and a gated ML benchmark; it remains active, with no duplicate goal created. The bounded finding is that female *Spodoptera littoralis* oviposition choices changed with playback of drought-stressed tomato-plant clicks, and the preference changed direction when real plants were present. A deafening control removed the plant-free playback preference; a male-moth-click control produced no detected preference. Main choice experiments played 60 clicks/min; a lower 30-click/min long-arena experiment used one moth per arena and a different setup. The authors explicitly describe the plant emissions as likely cues rather than evolved messages. This is one species/plant pair in controlled settings; the reviewer exchange discusses ecological realism, effect presentation, data availability and generalization limits.

## October 13 continuation — parrot detection evidence and model boundary

**Question:** is a useful first ML step for the Field Companion acoustic event detection, and does existing parrot work support translation claims?

**Evidence reviewed:** selected sections of the peer-reviewed ANIMAL-SPOT paper (abstract, task/data methods, Tables 1 and 3, and relevant results/discussion), official repository README/license/split guidance, and MPG.PuRe article/dataset metadata. The paper reports distinct target/noise and monk-parakeet call-type tasks; the latter covers alarm/contact/other plus noise. It reports 92.7% accuracy on human-labeled test samples and 88.4% on machine-selected segments. The repository describes grouping excerpts from the same year/tape when creating splits. Individual/animal grouping and the exact data archive were not verified.

The practical app lesson is to expose a sound/call category only as a reviewable hypothesis and keep it separate from observed context. No app classifier was added.

## October 13 continuation — full-paper review sharpens the ANIMAL-SPOT benchmark question

**Question:** what does the primary paper actually support about held-out performance, and what can the Edmond monk-parakeet deposit test?

**Evidence reviewed:** read the complete publisher article text, including methods for preprocessing and data partitioning, the target/noise and call-type experiments, results, discussion, and ethics/data-collection description; revisited Tables 1 and 3 and the official ANIMAL-SPOT split guidance. The paper says samples from any one recording stay in a single partition, with a default 70/15/15 train/validation/test split. It reports mean test-set accuracy of 97.9% (range 94.5–99.8%) and, separately, 95.9% average AUC (range 91.7–99.1%) across 33 additional unseen animal-specific recordings. Monk-parakeet call-type accuracy is 92.7% on human-labeled test examples and 88.4% on detector-selected segments. The paper does not establish that individual animals are held out. The supplement's split tables and exact Edmond archive remain uninspected.

**Decision and change:** updated the source note and resource ledger to separate recording-held-out evaluation from animal-held-out generalization. The only defensible candidate is a reproduction of monk-parakeet target/noise performance on the exact V2.0 deposit and its recording-level split, reported per held-out recording. An individual-held-out claim is a separate question, possible only if the archive has suitable identity metadata and a specialist approves the grouping. This remains a proposal, not an approved run; Edmond terms were not accepted, no data or code was acquired or executed, and AutoResearch remains **NOT READY**.

## October 14 — budgerigar playback-context evidence note

**Question:** can playback change parrot vocal output, and what does that imply for Talk2Nature's passive phone workflow?

**Evidence reviewed:** Seki and Dooling (2016), *Effect of auditory stimuli on conditioned vocal behavior of budgerigars* (DOI 10.1016/j.beproc.2015.11.002). Reviewed the PubMed citation/abstract and selected PMC author-manuscript sections surfaced by the article index: subjects, apparatus, stimuli, procedures, analyses, and results/discussion. The listed supplement, raw data and code were not inspected. No reanalysis, replication or independent review was performed.

**Finding and boundary:** five individually housed budgerigars (one male, four females) were operantly trained to call after a visual cue. Calls in the call-plus-flock condition were louder than in the comparison conditions; only three birds produced the non-primary calls used in the call-variation result. This is evidence that acoustic context can alter conditioned vocal output in this setup. It does not test message meaning, receiver comprehension, consumer apps or ordinary household behavior. The small sample, fixed condition sequence and training limit generalization. The paper reports an institutional animal-care approval and a restricted-weight protocol; that protocol is not consumer-app guidance. Keep public playback disabled.

**Change and rights:** added research note `budgerigar-playback-context`, source 312, metadata-only resource `budgerigar-conditioned-vocal-output-seki-dooling-2016`, and a link from the meaning-learning path. Article reuse terms and data/code rights remain unverified; no article, supplement, data, audio or code was acquired.

The local noindex build produced 108 pages plus 404; the checker validated 109 HTML documents and 5,308 links. (2023), *Anterior forebrain pathway in parrots is necessary for producing learned vocalizations with individual signatures*, *Current Biology* 33(24):5415–5426.e4, DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2023.11.014, PMCID PMC10799565. Reviewed the full PMC text through NCBI E-utilities, including behavior paradigm, VAE/SVM methods, results, discussion, animal-care and data/code statements. Cross-checked the article's Mendeley v1 reference against the existing versioned resource and previous checksum-pinned one-file inspection. No new article/data file was retained; no code/model was run, no reanalysis or independent review was performed.

**Finding:** eight budgerigars in the contact-call cohort produced 180–1,612 calls per bird per day in response to colony-noise playback. A VAE plus SVM classified caller identity above 90% in a balanced, random 80/20 call-level split repeated 50 times; accuracy stayed around 90% for two call types shared across birds. Cross-time prediction from week 3 to week 15 dropped from about 90% to 40%. In a separate five-bird experiment, birds continued responding to individual calls during AFP inactivation, though response rate fell in three birds and latency changes varied. The neural intervention also altered call acoustics and reduced individual discriminability. The study supports acoustic signatures and a production mechanism in its laboratory setup; it does not decode call meaning.

**Evaluation, rights and decision:** the identity split holds birds in both train and test data, so the score does not establish performance on unseen birds, sites, devices or species. The work used captive birds, controlled loudspeaker playback, specialized microphones and invasive neural procedures. The paper's PMC notice permits text mining/fair-use use but is not an open redistribution license; its Mendeley data deposit has a separate CC BY 4.0 declaration, while custom scripts are available from the lead contact without a verified public license. Updated the existing research note/source and added a separate paper resource record. Keep the existing one-file sample exploratory: sample rate `44101` and file-to-caller/session/condition mapping remain unresolved. AutoResearch remains **NOT READY**; do not use this study as an unseen-bird or call-meaning benchmark.

**Verification:** 140 Python tests and 115 Node tests passed; the source catalog validates 141 resources. The explicit-origin public build produced 110 pages plus 404, and the site checker validated 111 HTML files, 5,538 links and all 110 public routes. The new evidence page has its canonical URL and `index,follow` metadata, links to the PMC article, and visibly states the held-out-bird limitation; the research-resource directory includes the paper record. These are build and crawl checks, not live deployment or search-engine indexing evidence.

They do not include independently observed receiver response or ground truth about meaning. The dataset is bird-focused but not a parrot context corpus; keep it separate from the proposed companion-parrot observation study.

**Rights and quality limits:** the record declares CC BY 4.0 for soundscape audio and dataset metadata/annotations. `train_xenocanto` retains source-record licenses, and the schema says some of those fields are empty. Version 1.1 marks 40 zero-area annotations unsuitable for detection/localization and documents one truncated Xeno-Canto file. Its test labels are public, so if examined for development, reserve a separate untouched evaluation. No per-row license review, group/source-overlap audit or qualified specialist review was performed.

## October 23 — prioritize the first communication-adjacent ML candidate

**Question:** which available animal dataset is the strongest first ML candidate for Talk2Nature's behavior/context question, rather than a generic detector?

**Evidence reviewed:** rechecked the five-page EUSIPCO 2024 paper and its 2017 Egyptian-fruit-bat data source alongside the current resource catalog, aggregate annotation report and methods-review packet. The paper describes 35,074 retained vocalizations in 11 video-coded context classes and three subject-independent development/test folds. Its within-development train/validation split is stratified by class but not identity. It reports pooled UAR of 22.4% (SVM), 27.7% (ResNet-50) and 33.3% (EfficientNet-B0); confidence intervals resample individual examples rather than animal/session clusters. The source archive reports 293,238 short 250 kHz WAV files and 91,080 annotations. The complete annotation table is already acquired locally and audited in aggregate; no bat audio, exact paper folds or FileInfo.csv was acquired or inspected.

**Decision and change:** updated `docs/BENCHMARK_CANDIDATE_RUN_CARD.md`, `docs/RESEARCHER_START.md`, `README.md` and the research backlog. Bat interaction-context prediction is now the first communication-adjacent ML candidate for independent review, not a ready-to-run benchmark. CEB remains a separate bird sound-event detection exercise, and monk-parakeet identity/convergence remains a separate task. The phone-first public study is still provisionally parrot-centered if multiple households and an avian researcher are available; the bat data was recorded with specialized ultrasonic equipment. New bat acquisition and model execution remain gated.

**Limits and next gate:** subject-independent folds are reported but not verified; both interaction roles, animal pairs, sessions, channels, dates, treatments and chamber conditions may affect generalization. The model predicts human video-coded context, not receiver comprehension or meaning. The next gate is independent bat-behavior and ML evaluation review of the estimand and minimum grouping/join artifacts. CEB's group audit is now secondary unless pursuing that detector task. No external reviewer was contacted, no model was run, and no deployment occurred. AutoResearch remains **NOT READY**.

**Question:** can a large bird-audio database provide a credible first machine-learning step for Talk2Nature?

The card dates its Xeno-Canto snapshot to 2024-03-10. These figures describe the upstream benchmark, not Talk2Nature results. Its labels address species and acoustic events; they do not establish animal comprehension or meaning.

No article body, audio, labels, code or weights were acquired or run. No training admission or commercial use is approved. The card also has conflicting dataset-version compatibility notes and its live viewer cannot load the custom dataset script; exact revision and location-field handling need review before any future acquisition.

**Project decision:** retain BirdSet as a methods reference for an acoustic perception layer, not as the first communication benchmark and not as a parrot-context dataset. **Decision and limits:** no site-code change or repeat submission is justified by this evidence. Leave the existing request in place and recheck after Google's processing/retry window; if the report still fails, repeat the live check and inspect any new, specific error before changing the site. Google's [Sitemaps report guidance](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7451001) says the report shows the latest submitted-request status, a fetch failure can have transient causes, and a live URL Inspection test is the way to confirm crawl permission and page fetch. The live check does not prove Google has processed the sitemap or indexed its 115 URLs. ## October 23 — zebra-finch dataset candidate screened

**Question:** is there a usable public dataset with enough ground truth to begin a testable animal-communication research task?

**Evidence reviewed:** the V33DA dataset card and file listing at pinned Hugging Face revision `975ddf36a1f0c0bffc512bf2c2e6aa40bb2a1913`. The card describes 33,625 caller-attributed events from 10 individually identified zebra finches, across three experiments and 16 recording days, with synchronized audio, video, pose and telemetry. It says caller truth was derived from on-body accelerometers and lists CC BY 4.0. The provider reports 18.8 GB. The dataset card marks its associated manuscript as under review. No files, code or models were acquired, inspected or run.

**Decision:** add V33DA as a metadata-only candidate for one bounded technical task: attribute an already-detected, isolated call to a visible bird, excluding accelerometer channels from model inputs and retaining them only as oracle truth. This can test caller attribution, not call meaning, behavioral context, receiver understanding or conversation. An unseen-bird split is essential; the card's held-out-experiment regime changes bird identity, group, date and cage together, so it cannot identify which shift caused any performance change.

**Limits and next gate:** the 33,625 events are nested within only 10 animals and one aviary/recording geometry; overlapping calls are excluded from the main benchmark. CC BY 4.0 is the repository's declaration, not an independent audit of each audio/video component or a legal opinion about commercial reuse. Verify component notices, rights, group identifiers and frozen split membership before acquisition or training. No biological result, independent reproduction or project model result is claimed. The mobile app remains passive-only; no playback or treatment experiment is authorized by this dataset review.

## October 23 — bat auditory-cortex vocal-production study

**Question:** what does a recent bat-neuroscience paper add to the project’s research map, and is its archive a candidate for our first audio benchmark?

**Evidence reviewed:** the full main text of Babl, Röhrig and Hechavarría (2026) through PMC, including sample, synchronized neural/acoustic methods, category definitions, main analyses, discussion, data/code statement and article license; and the public GIN DOI landing page. The paper reports ten awake *Carollia perspicillata* bats, 32 sessions, 631 selected vocal events and 396 neuronal units. Neural activity was associated with call class and sequence complexity around the animals’ own vocal production. Pre-vocal activity tracked social-call syllable count; the echolocation pulse-count relationship appeared after vocal onset. The reported SVM used randomized call-event-by-neuron instances; the reviewed methods do not establish held-out-animal or held-out-session performance. This is self-production neurophysiology, not receiver comprehension or a call-meaning result.

**Provenance and limits:** the paper is CC BY 4.0. The GIN record lists a 5.8 GiB archive containing neural and acoustic data and declares CC BY-SA 4.0 at repository level. We did not inspect the archive manifest, file members, code, dependencies or supplementary files. Those rights and components remain separate. No recording, archive, code or model was acquired, executed or reproduced; no independent specialist reviewed the Talk2Nature assessment. This is comparative neuroscience material, not a practical phone-capture design or a candidate for the first audio/context benchmark.

**Change:** added one source-grounded research note, separate paper/data/code resource records and source records 368–369; added this reading to `docs/RESEARCH_BACKLOG.md`. All records remain metadata-only. AutoResearch remains **NOT READY**.

## October 23 — budgerigar edge-monitoring prior art

**Question:** has a long-running dedicated listening device already been used to monitor parrot vocal activity, and what would remain distinctive for Talk2Nature?

**Evidence reviewed:** Agishev et al., *Edge-Based Long-Term Automated Monitoring of Budgerigar Vocal Activity Using YAMNet*, *Animals* 16(20), 3246, DOI 10.3390/ani16203246. Reviewed the publisher early-access record and abstract only; the publisher's full-page request was rate-limited and the record says complete PDF/HTML/XML versions will follow. The abstract reports ten budgerigars monitored under stable housing from June 2025 to May 2026, local Raspberry Pi processing with YAMNet features and a task-specific binary classifier, and a one-second vocal-activity measure. Detailed validation, false-positive rates, ethics, data availability, code and model terms remain unreviewed.

**Decision and rights:** continuous edge-based vocal-activity monitoring is prior art, so Talk2Nature should not present a listening station or activity counter alone as novel. The study does not, from the abstract reviewed, establish caller identity, context, receiver response or call meaning. The publisher displays an Open Access label, but the exact article license and all data/code/model rights remain unresolved. No files, audio or weights were acquired or run. Added one abstract-level evidence note and separate paper resource; the device/app cohort remains distinct from the current ML benchmark candidates.

## October 23 — choose a first dataset by scientific objective

**Comparison reviewed:** the Great Tit Song Dataset paper describes 109,963 annotated songs, over 1.1 million acoustic units and more than 400 birds; its value is population-scale song structure, not receiver response or meaning. The ZF-AIM v3 preprint abstract reports over 1,000 hours of female zebra-finch vocal interactions and AI-mediated playback experiments. Its linked Zenodo record lists 26.6 GB and states MIT for code and weights, but the data/recording license is unclear; methods and archive inventory remain unreviewed. These are two different scientific opportunities, not a single interchangeable “big dataset.”

**Decision:** propose Great Tit as the first bounded, population-scale audio-methods exercise, after exact OSF files, rights/privacy scope and a non-duplicative question are checked. Prioritize full methods and component-rights review of ZF-AIM as the more communication-relevant turn-taking lead. Keep V33DA++ for overlap/activity engineering; it uses the same ten zebra finches as V33DA and is not an independent animal cohort. Keep Kiki/parrot app work in the product/usability lane. No recordings, code, weights or data archives were acquired or executed, no model or playback was run, and no acquisition or training is authorized by this comparison. The sequence is recorded in `docs/FIRST_ANIMAL_PLAN.md`.

## October 23 — ZF-AIM full-text review and first-species decision

Reviewed the full main text of the bioRxiv v3 zebra-finch ZF-AIM study, including its interaction and model methods, results, discussion, and version-specific data-availability statement. It reports more than 1,000 hours of female vocal interactions and analyzes 834,309 calls. A response is defined as the first call within one second after a partner call ends. The paper reports acoustic response/covariation and task-specific next-caller, next-token and wait-time prediction; this is evidence about contingent acoustic patterns, not translated semantic content. The report of 20 birds in one Results passage conflicts with 21 in Methods. Evaluation is described by pair, but bird-level disjointness is not established in the reviewed paper.

The official Zenodo record lists a 26.6 GB archive, a record-level MIT field, and a description that states code and weights are MIT. Its exact file manifest and audio/benchmark-data rights remain unresolved. The archive and supplements were not inspected or acquired; no model was run. The preprint's release statement and later Zenodo record are version/timing-specific and not reconciled. Added a source-linked research note, updated its metadata-only resource record, and refreshed the first-animal plan and backlog.

**Recommendation:** continue treating Great Tit as the population-scale song-structure methods candidate, zebra-finch ZF-AIM as the most direct turn-taking literature lead, Egyptian fruit bat as a blocked context-prediction candidate pending group/split review, and parrots as the separate phone-app feasibility cohort. There is no single “largest dataset” that supports all these tasks. Do not start by training a general animal-language model.

## October 24 — separate a large-data starting point from a communication study

**Question:** is there a bird and public database where Talk2Nature can begin applying machine learning without overstating what the data show?

**Evidence reviewed:** reviewed the full methods of the 2025 great-tit song-culture paper and the authors' Wytham dataset documentation, alongside the October 23 OSF API manifest already recorded in `research/wytham_osf_manifest_2026-10-23.json`. The source reports 109,963 annotated songs, 1,161,033 acoustic units and more than 400 birds. The 2025 paper trained a ViT metric-learning model over the corpus and used embeddings for repertoire similarity and demographic culture analyses. The dataset labels song structure and repertoire, not independently observed interaction context or receiver response. The OSF node declares CC BY 4.0; its manifest contains nestbox metadata and a perimeter shapefile whose values and location sensitivity remain uninspected. Separately, the ZF-AIM data deposit has conflicting CC BY-SA and CC BY-NC declarations and does not yet establish full corpus coverage.

**Decision:** Great Tits are the strongest reviewed *large-data methods* starting point, but only for a scoped reproduction or a clearly distinct acoustic-structure question after independent review; generic embeddings, similarity or culture analysis would duplicate published work. Zebra finches are closer to a controlled exchange question, but ZF-AIM remains metadata-only until data terms, corpus scope and bird-level split independence are resolved. Budgerigars remain a separate possible household-app cohort, not a substitute public benchmark. No current candidate licenses a claim of decoded call meaning.

**Limits and next gate:** no Wytham payload was downloaded, no model was trained, no outside reviewer was contacted and no animal study was conducted. First review the exact proposed task, split and potentially sensitive metadata with independent avian-bioacoustics and evaluation specialists. Preserve the existing synthetic-only private intake gate; AutoResearch remains **NOT READY**.

## October 24 — correct the zebra-finch benchmark novelty boundary

**New evidence:** reviewed Figure 4 and its caption in Elie et al. (2025) and the authors' public repository README. The original paper already compares an acoustic-classifier confusion matrix with the finches' behavioral confusion matrix; the README describes spectrogram LDA confusion matrices from leave-one-vocalizer-out cross-validation. The 2026 BirdAVES paper classifies the call labels but, in the reviewed article, does not directly evaluate those predictions against the behavioral confusion matrix.

**Correction and next decision:** updated Candidate E, the research note/resource records and first-animal decision table. Basic model-versus-bird confusion alignment is prior art. The only candidate extension is whether a modern pretrained audio representation adds alignment beyond the published LDA and acoustic-similarity baselines on the same verified calls. The Bat rows remain unmapped and excluded from interpretation pending source clarification. Updated the existing moth research note and catalog entry; no duplicate research page was added. The sample remains in ignored local storage and is not in the website, Git, examples, private database or training data.

## October 25 — add a context-aware vervet study to the evidence library

**Question:** what does the vervet alarm-call literature teach about choosing an initial animal question and designing observations that do not mistake a signal for a translated word?

**Evidence:** reviewed the Wiley abstract and German summary for the 1980 developmental study, the ScienceDirect abstract for the longer 1980b playback paper, the 1980a Science PubMed abstract, selected full-text sections of Fischer (2020), and the full Springer article for Deshpande et al. (2023). The 2023 article reports eight adult female subjects from one group and 16 within-subject trials. Lower speaker-directed looking and vigilance were reported when a male alarm bark played during an ongoing intergroup encounter than when no encounter was underway; no predator-specific escape response occurred. The paper's Results and Discussion contradict each other on the direction of the startle effect, so this measure is unresolved. The article declares CC BY 4.0 for the paper and links data/code via OSF; those artifacts and their separate rights/privacy terms were not inspected.

**Change and decision:** updated the vervet note and source/resource catalog, and added the KwaZulu-Natal study region alongside Amboseli. The atlas deliberately omits the exact wildlife-site coordinates printed in the paper. Vervet literature is a useful context/receiver-response methods case, not a ready open benchmark or first phone cohort. Added this comparison to `docs/FIRST_DATASET_DECISION.md`; the public app remains species-neutral, and no animal cohort or model was selected.

**Validation and limits:** 172 Python tests passed with one intentional external-sample skip; all 122 Node tests passed; the collection validator accepted 223 resources. The local noindex build produced 138 pages plus 404; the checker validated 139 HTML documents and 7,120 links. The generated vervet route showed the updated title, 2023 citation, bounded findings and next-reading note. The owner-local SQLite catalog imported 757 public metadata records; an immediate repeat changed zero. `git diff --check` passed. No data, code, audio or model was acquired or run; no hosted database, external contact or deployment was involved. This is a source-led editorial and atlas update, not independent scientific review, a new experiment or evidence of animal communication.

**Evidence:** reviewed NLnet's current [GenAI policy v2.0](https://nlnet.nl/foundation/policies/generativeAI/2.0/), its [FAQ](https://nlnet.nl/foundation/policies/generativeAI/faq/), its [October 20 applicability notice](https://nlnet.nl/news/2026/20261020-AI-policy.html), and the [CodeSupply eligibility rules](https://nlnet.nl/codesupply/eligibility/). Restack remains out of scope because the project has no evidence of the one-million-active-user threshold or a stack-relevant work package. No proposal was generated, drafted, submitted or discussed with NLnet.

## October 26 — add a bounded cockatiel receiver-response reference while keeping zero-command gates open

**Question:** can a controlled parrot study improve Talk2Nature's measurement design without encouraging an unsafe app behavior or a general translation claim?

**Evidence reviewed:** the full primary [PLOS ONE article](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0205314), including its ethics statement, methods, results, discussion and supporting-information manifest. The study tested ten captive cockatiels with partner distress calls, familiar non-partner calls and white noise on separate days. During playback, partner and non-partner distress calls each increased call counts relative to white noise, but partner versus non-partner call counts did not differ (p=.37). Partner-versus-nonpartner movement was marginal (p=.07), and one crest-posture comparison was p=.05. The partner-call loudspeaker-distance comparison could not be tested because no bird spent more than 15 seconds near the speaker. The article page states CC BY 4.0 for the article and lists S1 Data as an XLSX. The XLSX was not downloaded or inspected; its file-specific reuse terms were not separately verified.

**Change:** added one source-grounded research note, two source records and separate paper/data resource entries. The article is a controlled receiver-response methods comparator, not a translation result, ML benchmark or claim about subjective animal states. The paper describes brief glove-associated restraint to elicit distress calls and controlled playback; those methods are explicitly excluded from the passive companion-app path. The S1 Data workbook remains metadata-only with unresolved rights. Budgerigars remain the provisional household-app cohort; cockatiels are a separate option only if access and independent avian review support it. Updated the first-animal plan, research backlog and active goal.

## October 27 continuation — deepen the great-tit receiver-response record

**Question:** what does the Carolina-wren playback study actually measure, what alternative explanation limits its sequence claim, and what separate data asset does it expose?

**Evidence reviewed:** publisher-indexed primary article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Ethical Note, Data Availability and Supplementary Material listing) plus the [University of Western Australia article record](https://research-repository.uwa.edu.au/en/publications/mobbing-sequences-of-american-wrens-elicit-mobbing-responses-in-e). The direct ScienceDirect page still returned HTTP 403, so no article file, figures or supplement bytes were opened.

**Finding:** the article reports 96 wild great tits, one playback each across six treatments. Call playback increased approach relative to controls, but call treatments did not differ significantly. Wing-flicking was more likely after FME–D sequences than after D-only calls or controls; the interspecies sequence comparison was nonsignificant and imprecise. The authors identify unmatched acoustic content/duty cycle as an alternative explanation: the FME–D sequence contains more material than the D-only playback, with no matched D-only condition. Carolina-wren stimuli were built from four source birds but only two tracks per treatment; no reversed-order Carolina-wren sequence was tested. The authors' ethics statement is recorded as their account, not a project protocol or independent welfare review.

**Data and rights decision:** the publisher says study data are in Supplementary Material and lists one 985-byte text file. Added source record 464 and a separate metadata-only dataset resource; its filename, bytes, contents and file-specific terms remain unknown. The UWA record links the paper under CC BY 4.0; that does not clear the supplementary file's exact terms or the separate Macaulay Library/Xeno-Canto stimulus recordings. Nothing was acquired, opened, played or analyzed. The article note and prioritized backlog now include these limits. Keep the app passive; do not treat receiver behavior as translation.

**Next:** the physical-phone save/reopen gate and authorized newcomer walkthrough remain open. Continue with accessible primary-source review or reproducibility improvements while waiting for device evidence. The five-track goal stays active; AutoResearch and real-data admission remain **NOT READY**.
